what_this_is: one index over what Dula already holds. It acquires nothing and computes no new value. Each record is projected from a source record into one shape that carries geography, period, unit, source and evidence state.

components.FLOW: movement, exchange, production, consumption and investment
components.CONSTRAINT: conditions affecting feasibility and productive activity
components.CAPABILITY: activities the economy can actually perform
components.DYNAMIC: shocks, responses, transmission, adaptation and feedback

evidence_classes.OBSERVED: a source reports this value for this thing, geography and period
evidence_classes.ACCOUNTING_IDENTITY: true by construction from its definition; carries no empirical content
evidence_classes.DERIVED: computed from observed inputs by a stated recipe
evidence_classes.ESTIMATED: inferred, with a stated basis that is weaker than observation
evidence_classes.PROXY_ONLY: a different thing is observed and stands in; the substitution is recorded
evidence_classes.HYPOTHESIS: proposed and not yet tested against evidence
evidence_classes.UNKNOWN: not observed, and no proxy is claimed

variable_is_not_an_object: employment is a measurement; an employer is an ACTOR; a wage is a FLOW; a skill is a productive resource; an employment relationship is a RELATIONSHIP. The 107 variables in machines.json are indexed as MEASUREMENTS and are deliberately not poured into the object components, where they would look like stocks and flows and be neither.

records.name: Rio Grande basin reservoir storage
records.source: Bureau of Reclamation (not acquired: see pipeline/wm3_acquire.py for the three attempts)
records.limitations: NOT ACQUIRED. Without it the water balance cannot be closed, and the model cannot say whether a dry year drew down storage or was buffered by it.
records.why_it_matters: Storage is the buffer that decides whether a poor snow year becomes a delivery shortfall this year or next.

records.name: Snow water equivalent, Upper Rio Grande stations
records.limitations: Two point stations, not a basin-integrated product. A seasonal stock: it is zero for months by design, so its level is only meaningful within a water year.
records.why_it_matters: The winter stock that becomes the following spring's flow — the clearest stock-to-flow relationship the model holds.

records.name: Antecedent soil moisture, Upper Rio Grande
records.source: SNOTEL soil-moisture sensors and modelled products (not acquired)
records.limitations: NOT ACQUIRED. It is the main reason a given snowpack yields different runoff in different years, so its absence is why snowpack → runoff has no coefficient.
records.why_it_matters: The hidden stock that explains runoff efficiency.

records.name: Groundwater in the study area's aquifers
records.unit: feet of water level, or acre-feet
records.source: USGS and NM OSE well records (not acquired at study-area resolution)
records.limitations: NOT ACQUIRED. Without it, groundwater substitution can be described but its consequence cannot be observed.
records.why_it_matters: The stock that adaptation draws down: pumping solves this season and may raise the cost of the next drought.

records.name: Total bank credit outstanding
records.source: Federal Reserve H.8 via FRED, weekly
records.limitations: National, and a stock of balances rather than of new lending: its level can rise while new origination falls.
records.why_it_matters: Credit is a stock that changes slowly; a rate change alters the flow into it long before the level moves.

records.name: Commercial and industrial loans outstanding
records.limitations: National; nothing distinguishes a small northern New Mexico borrower from a national corporate one.
records.why_it_matters: The business-credit stock behind the small-business availability question.

records.name: Consumer credit outstanding
records.source: Federal Reserve G.19 via FRED, monthly
records.limitations: National. Neither a subset of ST_BANK_CREDIT nor independent of it; the two may not be added.
records.why_it_matters: Household balance-sheet state, which conditions how a cost shock is absorbed.

records.name: Housing units in the eight study counties
records.source: domain:housing (ACS/Census; the domain holds the figure and its caveats)
records.limitations: The domain's own evidence, read-only here. Units are not habitable units, and the count moves for enumeration reasons as well as physical ones (housing HU03).
records.why_it_matters: The stock that a construction response would change — very slowly. Annual additions are a small fraction of it.

records.name: US crude oil and product inventories
records.source: EIA weekly stocks (not acquired: no FRED CSV id resolves; the EIA API needs a key)
records.limitations: NOT ACQUIRED. Inventories are the short-run buffer between a supply disruption and a price move, so without them the energy machine cannot distinguish a shock that was absorbed from one that was passed through.
records.why_it_matters: The single most important missing stock in the energy machine.

records.name: Household financial assets
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) table B.101 via FRED
records.limitations: National, and an aggregate over roughly 130 million households plus nonprofit organizations. It contains no distribution, so it cannot say which households hold any of it.
records.why_it_matters: The stock that household saving accumulates into, and the one a household draws on when income falls. Without it, saving is a flow into nothing.

records.name: Household real estate at market value
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) via FRED
records.limitations: A value, not a housing stock. National.
records.why_it_matters: The largest asset most households that hold any asset hold, and the collateral behind most household borrowing.

records.name: Household liabilities
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) via FRED
records.limitations: National aggregate. The same total is consistent with widely-held small debts and with concentrated large ones.
records.why_it_matters: What households owe, which is what turns an income change into a constraint rather than an inconvenience.

records.name: Household one-to-four-family mortgage debt
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) via FRED
records.limitations: National.
records.why_it_matters: The debt secured against ST_HH_REAL_ESTATE: the pair is what makes the household balance sheet a circuit rather than two lists.

records.name: Nonfinancial corporate business assets
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) table B.103 via FRED
records.limitations: Corporate only: it excludes unincorporated business entirely, which is how most firms in the study area are organised. National.
records.why_it_matters: The productive-asset stock the exam found missing. Investment flows into it, depreciation out of it, and what remains is what the economy can produce with.

records.name: Nonfinancial corporate business liabilities
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) via FRED
records.limitations: National, corporate only.
records.why_it_matters: Who has a claim on the firm sector. Section 10's question about where returns go begins here.

records.name: Nonfinancial corporate business debt securities and loans
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) via FRED
records.limitations: National. Says nothing about maturity or about fixed versus floating rate, which is what decides whether a policy rate change reaches an existing borrower at all.
records.why_it_matters: The debt the firm sector actually owes, separated from an equity valuation that dominates the total and moves for unrelated reasons.

records.name: Nonfinancial corporate equity claims outstanding
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) via FRED
records.limitations: National. It does not say who holds the claims, and ownership is not domicile.
records.why_it_matters: The ownership claim on productive assets: v0.2's distinction between owning an asset and being able to produce needs both stocks to exist, and this is the second one.

records.name: Nonfinancial noncorporate business assets
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) table B.104 via FRED
records.limitations: Noncorporate is a legal form, not a size: large partnerships are inside it and incorporated one-person firms are outside it. National.
records.why_it_matters: The sector most of the study area's firms belong to, and the one every corporate aggregate in this model excludes.

records.name: Nonfinancial noncorporate business liabilities
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) via FRED
records.limitations: National. The link that matters most here is absent from every published account: unincorporated business debt is often secured on the owner's house, and nothing observes that.
records.why_it_matters: The debt of the firms whose owner's balance sheet and firm's balance sheet are the same balance sheet.

records.name: Deposits at commercial banks
records.source: Federal Reserve H.8 via FRED, weekly
records.limitations: National. Reclassifications when an institution changes charter move the level with no deposit being made or withdrawn.
records.why_it_matters: The matched liability of bank lending. PIERCE-08 had to record FL_CREDIT_CREATION's counterparty as created OUTSIDE the modelled stock set; this is the stock that brings it inside.

records.name: Real estate loans at commercial banks
records.limitations: National, and only the bank-held share: most residential mortgage debt is not held by banks.
records.why_it_matters: The largest component of bank credit, and the join between the credit circuit and the housing circuit.

records.name: Consumer loans at commercial banks
records.limitations: National, and the bank-held share only.
records.why_it_matters: This is the stock that MEASURES the overlap PIERCE-14 could only name: ST_CONSUMER_CREDIT (G.19, all holders) against this (banks only). The difference is the nonbank share.

records.name: Domestic financial sector total financial assets
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) via FRED
records.limitations: Includes banks, and double-counts claims between financial institutions. It is an APPROACH to nonbank credit, not a measurement of it.
records.why_it_matters: The only handle this model has on the intermediary sector as a whole, and therefore on the counter-mechanism that keeps appearing on credit edges: lenders that are not banks.

records.name: Domestic financial sector debt securities and loans
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) via FRED
records.limitations: National; excludes deposits, which are a different liability.
records.why_it_matters: The leverage of the intermediaries themselves, which is why their behaviour changes when funding costs move.

records.name: Federal government debt securities and loans
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) via FRED
records.limitations: A different definition from the Treasury's total public debt, which is also held (world:GFDEBTN). The difference is debt the government owes itself.
records.why_it_matters: The stock the fiscal flows accumulate into. The model observed federal spending and receipts and held no stock they changed.

records.name: State and local government debt securities and loans
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts (Z.1) via FRED
records.limitations: A national aggregate of fifty states and tens of thousands of local governments. It is NOT New Mexico and must never be read as it.
records.why_it_matters: The level of government that builds most public infrastructure, and the one a place's own fiscal position sits inside.

records.name: US net international investment position
records.source: Bureau of Economic Analysis international accounts via FRED
records.limitations: National. A place has no equivalent, and the model must not invent one.
records.why_it_matters: The boundary condition section 9 insists on. Claims and returns can leave, and this is the stock that records that they have.

records.name: Snow accumulation
records.recipe: positive day-to-day changes in station SWE
records.limitations: Station-level; not a basin water volume.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Snowmelt
records.recipe: negative day-to-day changes in station SWE
records.limitations: Melt and sublimation are not separated, so this overstates the water that reaches the ground. Nor does all melt infiltrate: some runs off directly over frozen or saturated ground, and that split is not observed.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Sublimation
records.limitations: NOT MEASURED, and in this climate it is a large term. It is one reason snowpack → runoff cannot be a coefficient.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Runoff to the river
records.source: USGS gauge discharge (the observable end of it)
records.limitations: Gauge discharge is what arrived, not what was generated; diversions and reservoir operations sit in between.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Reservoir inflow
records.limitations: NOT ACQUIRED with the storage it fills.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Reservoir release
records.limitations: NOT ACQUIRED. The gauge below El Vado shows the consequence of releases, not the release decision.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Reservoir evaporation
records.limitations: NOT ACQUIRED.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.limitations: Statewide monthly totals; a watershed's timing and intensity are not resolved.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Evapotranspiration
records.limitations: NOT ACQUIRED. Temperature is observed and is a driver, but the flux itself is not held.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.limitations: NOT ACQUIRED.

records.name: Household borrowing
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts via FRED
records.recipe: change in the outstanding household debt level between quarters
records.limitations: A NET flow: new borrowing minus repayment and charge-offs. It cannot be read as origination.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Household debt extinguished
records.limitations: NOT PUBLISHED separately. Only the net change in the level is observable, so repayment, refinancing and charge-off cannot be told apart.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Net addition to household real estate value
records.limitations: NOT OBSERVED as a flow. Residential investment (world:PRFI) is the nearest published quantity and it is not this: it is spending on construction and improvement, not the change in the sector's holdings, and it excludes the land.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Business fixed investment
records.source: BEA private nonresidential fixed investment via FRED
records.limitations: PNFI covers ALL private nonresidential investment, corporate and noncorporate together, while the stock it is written against is corporate only. The two do not match and the difference is not separated in any published series this model holds.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Consumption of fixed capital
records.source: BEA consumption of fixed capital, private, via FRED
records.limitations: An ESTIMATE using assumed service lives, not an observation. Private rather than corporate, so it does not match the stock exactly.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Undistributed corporate profits
records.source: BEA net private saving: domestic business: undistributed corporate profits, via FRED
records.limitations: Heavily revised, and it arrives with tax data years later.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Distribution to holders of claims
records.recipe: corporate profits after tax (world:CPATAX) minus undistributed corporate profits (world:B057RC1Q027SBEA)
records.limitations: The two series are not drawn on identical definitions — CPATAX carries inventory and capital consumption adjustments and covers all corporations — so the difference is an approximation of distributions, not a published figure. It also goes to holders who are not households: pension funds, other firms, and the rest of the world.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Net corporate borrowing
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts via FRED
records.recipe: change in the outstanding debt securities and loans level between quarters
records.limitations: NET. It cannot be read as issuance, and it says nothing about maturity or about whether the rate is fixed or floating — which decides whether a policy rate change reaches an existing borrower at all.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Net corporate equity issuance
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts, corporate equities liability transactions, via FRED
records.limitations: NET of retirements. It is persistently NEGATIVE, which means the sector retires more equity than it issues, and a negative inflow is a statement about the direction of the circuit rather than an error in it.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Net deposit creation
records.recipe: change in the outstanding deposit level between periods
records.limitations: A NET flow. Deposits are also created by inflows from outside the banking system and destroyed by repayment, and H.8 nets all of it.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Net federal borrowing
records.source: Federal Reserve Financial Accounts via FRED
records.recipe: change in the outstanding federal debt securities and loans level between quarters
records.limitations: NET of redemption. Debt-limit suspensions move issuance between periods with no fiscal change.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Net external financing
records.limitations: NOT ACQUIRED. The financial account of the balance of payments is published and is not held here. Most of the CHANGE in the stock is revaluation rather than this flow, so using the level change as a proxy for it would be wrong by more than the flow itself.
records.systems_basis: inherited from the stock it changes; a flow record carries no machine key

records.name: Business formation
records.unit: establishment entries, and firm births where they are distinguished
records.cross_cutting: business formation happens in every productive system and is specific to none
records.output: new businesses that begin operating in the region and are still operating a year later
records.conditions: counted where the business is located, including nonemployer businesses where the source permits

records.name: Business ownership transfer
records.cross_cutting: ownership transfer is not itself a productive system
records.output: operating businesses that change ownership and continue operating afterwards
records.conditions: the operation continues after the change; an asset sale that ends the operation is not a transfer

records.name: Business expansion
records.cross_cutting: expansion is an action a firm in any system takes
records.output: existing businesses that add productive capacity — a site, a line, a shift or a facility
records.conditions: an addition that increases what the business can produce or serve, distinguished from replacing what it already had

records.name: Building trades and crews available to work in the region
records.source: QCEW specialty-trade establishments, region 681 (2019) → 665 (2024); nonemployer construction 2,745 (2018) → 2,861 (2022)
records.proxy_note: Establishment and nonemployer counts observe REGISTERED BUSINESS UNITS, not people, crews, hours or availability. They do not distinguish a one-person remodeler from a framing crew of eight, and they say nothing about whether anyone will travel to Mora. Housing rule HR15 states this directly: a count of builders is not capacity.

records.name: Firms that can take a housing project from site to occupancy
records.source: New single-family general contractors, region 228 (2019) → 197 (2024); new multifamily GCs suppressed at region level
records.proxy_note: An establishment is a location, not a developer with the balance sheet, staff and financing relationships to deliver a project. The count does not distinguish a remodeler from a production builder, and a suppressed figure is unknown, not zero (HR07).

records.name: Land with water, wastewater and road service and the capacity to add homes
records.observation_required: A serviced-land inventory by jurisdiction distinguishing the four states Housing already defines in R-INFRA: UTILITY NEARBY / SERVICE AVAILABLE / CAPACITY AVAILABLE / CAPACITY ECONOMICALLY VIABLE. Sources are named and none is ingested: NMED Drinking Water Bureau sanitary surveys and capacity-development reviews by system id; municipal utility master plans and 40-year water plans; OSE water-right permits by system; NMED liquid-waste permits by county.

records.name: Spare connection capacity in community water and wastewater systems
records.source: EPA SDWIS, retrieved 2026-09-19: 210 active community water systems across the eight counties, 161,122 service connections, 373,733 population served; 160 of the systems serve under 500 people
records.observation_required: Per-system: permitted capacity, current demand, and the system's own statement of how many new connections it will accept and on what terms. NMED capacity-development reviews hold much of this and are obtainable by public-records request.

records.name: Zoning approval, entitlement and building permits

records.name: Building materials delivered to a regional job site

Subsidy and equity that closes the gap on a project that will not pencil
records.source: 1,775 tax-credit new-construction units awarded 2019–2026; statewide 9% total development cost per unit rose $198,557 (2014) → $316,938 (2024)
records.observation_required: Completion dates for the projects awarded since 2019 (HU14), and the disposition of unsuccessful applications (HU15). Both sit in MFA records.

records.name: Households able and willing to pay what a new unit costs
records.source: Half or more of renters are cost-burdened in five counties, including counties where rents are low (HC06); 14.1% of the region's units are vacant but only 1.8% are for rent or sale
records.proxy_note: Cost burden and vacancy describe the existing stock and existing households. Neither observes whether anyone would pay the cost of a NEW unit in a given place, which is the quantity HU06 asks for.

records.name: Architecture and engineering able to produce a permittable set
records.source: QCEW NAICS 5413 establishments rose in every county with a reading: Santa Fe 122 → 150, Sandoval 53 → 72, Los Alamos 21 → 29, Taos 13 → 19 (2019 → 2024)
records.proxy_note: A count of architecture and engineering establishments, not of drawings produced, capacity to produce them, or willingness to take small rural jobs.
records.observation_required: Whether projects outside the two cities wait for, or go without, design capacity. HF11's project reconstruction would show it if it occurred.

records.name: People operating farms and ranches in the eight counties
records.source: Census of Agriculture: 8,869 producers on 4,757 operations (2022), down from 10,357 on 6,085 (2017); 4,255 producers aged 65+ and 1,606 aged 75+ (partial counts, floors); 519 under 35

records.name: Land in the region that is irrigated and in production
records.source: 64,256 irrigated acres (2022, partial floor), down from 106,271 (2017); Rio Arriba 21,304, Colfax 9,775, Taos 8,977, Santa Fe 6,742, Sandoval 6,599, Mora 6,028, San Miguel 4,831

records.name: Water actually delivered to irrigators and towns
records.source: the physical chain above it is well measured — 36 years of daily gauge data at four gauges, the full weekly Drought Monitor record, SNOTEL back to 1990 — but delivery itself is not
records.proxy_note: Streamflow, snowpack and drought category observe the BASIN, not what reaches a headgate. Phase 3 demonstrated the gap: across 30 water years the same inch of peak snowpack produced between 12.9 and 90.9 thousand acre-feet of April–July flow, a factor of seven. Physical water is not legally available water is not deliverable water.

records.name: Fuel, fertilizer and feed delivered to a regional farm
records.source: national fertilizer and diesel price indices; regional farm expense shares observed once, in the 2022 Census of Agriculture
records.proxy_note: National prices are not prices paid here. Gate G_FEED_BASIS — the basis between global benchmarks and feed delivered to the study area — is unobserved, as is G_P13, the diesel price actually paid in the eight counties.

records.name: Washing, packing and cooling between the field and a buyer
records.source: FY26 state grants name specific new capacity: Garcia Road Farm wash-pack and cold storage, Indigenous Farm Hub wash-pack and cold storage ($100,000), Dixon Cooperative Market cold storage and handling equipment, Bamboo Farms aggregation and cold storage
records.observation_required: For the commercial-core operations (the 332 with sales over $50k): what happens to product between field and buyer, what equipment is used, and what turned away volume.

records.name: Inspected slaughter and cut-and-wrap within reach of northern ranchers
records.source: three FSIS establishments in the study area, all classed Very Small — C4 Enterprises (Tierra Amarilla), Naturally New Mexico Food Products (El Rito), High Country Meats (Raton). None in Santa Fe, Taos or Los Alamos counties. The state inspection tier is authorised but not operating and documents no state-inspected establishments.
records.observation_required: U01, directly: weekly slaughter and cut-and-wrap capacity, current utilisation and booking lead time at C4, Naturally New Mexico and High Country Meats, plus U02 — what share of those slots go to northern ranchers rather than other customers. This is the single observation that would turn a stated rating into an effective capacity.

records.name: Cold storage between a northern farm and a northern buyer
records.source: near Santa Fe it is documented — The Kitchen Table rents walk-in cooler and freezer space, SFFMI placed five mobile cold trailers with farmers, the Food Depot runs a large regional operation. In the far north and northeast it was NOT FOUND IN THE SOURCES REVIEWED, and is being built farm by farm with FY26 grants.
records.observation_required: U10 and U32: an inventory of cold storage in the eight counties with monthly fullness and the terms on which spare space could be used — including whether the Food Depot has harvest-season slack.

records.name: Intermediaries that consolidate small northern lots into buyable volume
records.source: eight hubs and distributors in the NM Grown approved-supplier programme, flat across FY23–FY25; 141 producers sourced through them of 253 total; named operators include Squash Blossom, New Mexico Harvest, La Montañita's Albuquerque DC, Agri-Cultura Network and SFFMI
records.observation_required: U07: how much northern produce moves south to Albuquerque hubs and back north again, and U36: whether hubs take title or sell on consignment, and who carries spoilage and rejection risk.

records.name: Refrigerated delivery to dispersed buyers north of Santa Fe
records.source: the Food Depot's fleet covered over 400,000 miles in 2024 across nine northern counties and 150+ distribution sites; C4 Enterprises self-distributes inspected meat in a grant-funded refrigerated vehicle

records.name: Diesel at the price actually paid in the eight counties
records.source: national and PADD III retail diesel series, observed weekly
records.proxy_note: A national or Gulf Coast average is not a price paid at a pump in Questa. Gate G_P13 requires recorded pump and bulk-delivery prices at named locations in the study area on the same dates as the published series, and none has been collected.

records.name: The road network the northern loop runs on
records.source: the 262-mile Santa Fe–Española–Taos–Questa–Mora–Las Vegas loop is documented, with about 5.5 hours of driving before dwell time
records.observation_required: Whether any northern delivery route has actually been cut by closure, and for how long. Nothing records it.

records.name: Schools, senior centres and food banks buying regional product
records.source: FY25 NM Grown: K-12 $1,572,508 across 64 buyers, senior $1,277,450 across 51, early childhood $279,156 across 28

records.name: Public purchasing money that pays the gap between local and broadline price
records.source: NM Grown spending rose $1.93M (FY23) to $5.41M (FY25); Regional Farm to Food Bank is about 35% of NM Grown purchases at $4.1M over three years; the current state appropriation is one-year money running to June 2027; LFPA federal funding was eliminated in 2025

records.name: Certification, insurance, invoicing and pack standards a buyer requires
records.source: documented in specific cases — Squash Blossom requires insurance and its own wholesale price list; the NM Grown approved-supplier programme sets the paperwork; 19% of approved suppliers sold to no buyer at all in FY23–25, and 22% of farms did not
records.observation_required: U26: for growers who are approved suppliers but sold nothing, which specific requirement stopped each sale.

records.name: Full-line grocery in single-store valleys
records.source: 68 SNAP-authorised full-line grocers across the eight counties in 2025 — Santa Fe 24, Sandoval 15, Taos 9, Rio Arriba 7, San Miguel 5, Colfax 4, Los Alamos 4, Mora 0 — against 32 that ended authorisation since 2015
records.observation_required: U18 and U19: the operating condition of the remaining independent rural grocers — margins, freight share, equipment — and their ownership-transition position. U19 must be collected as owners' own statements, never inferred from age.

records.name: Owners of operating businesses who may exit
records.source: ABS 2022 owner-age shares: 39% of Santa Fe and 44% of Taos owners of employer firms are 65 or over, against 31% statewide
records.proxy_note: The source's own caution, kept verbatim in the model: these are counts of OWNERS of employer firms, not firms; owner age says nothing about an individual owner's plans and cannot be attributed to any business. It bounds how large the population that may face a transition is. It measures no risk and no intent.

records.name: People able and willing to take over or start an operating business
records.observation_required: BU03 and BU19: where a transition is expected, whether a successor is identified and what stops it; and in transfers that succeeded, which features were necessary. BF01 (brokers) and BF13 are OUTREACH_READY for exactly this and nobody has been contacted.

records.name: Finance available to buy an operating business here
records.source: SBA 7(a) change-of-ownership loans in the region run at about 3–9 a year, recorded as a LOWER BOUND and coded only from FY2018
records.proxy_note: SBA-financed transfers are a floor on transfers, not all transfers — the model enforces this as rule R16. Bank, seller and cash transfers are invisible in it.

records.name: Brokers, accountants and lenders who make a transfer happen
records.source: brokers are reported to say there are more qualified buyers than sellable businesses, and that clean financials and low owner dependence are now prerequisites for closing a sale

records.name: Premises a business can occupy on terms it can meet
Money to start a business here
records.source: one documented channel built for northern food producers: SFFMI has made 379 microloans to 105 borrowers totalling $871,760 since 2008
records.observation_required: BU28-equivalent for formation: what credit is sought, declined and obtained by new businesses in the eight counties. The food domain's U28 asks the same for farm and food businesses via FSA, CDFIs and credit unions.

records.name: Technical assistance and business-support institutions
records.source: documented in one transfer: outside technical assistance was a feature of the single worker-cooperative conversion (BT-11)
records.observation_required: BU15: where employees are interested in ownership, what is missing — structure, finance, owner willingness or technical assistance. It can only come from the people involved.

records.name: Customers with money to spend in the region
records.source: county personal income by source (BEA) is the nearest observable, and the sensor for it is READY_TO_ACTIVATE and has never been run
records.proxy_note: Personal income is not spending in the region: it does not separate what is spent locally from what leaves, and it says nothing about demand for any particular business.

records.name: Workers a business can hire and keep
records.source: county unemployment rates are observed monthly; QWI job flows by firm age are observed to 2024
records.proxy_note: An unemployment rate observes people not working, not people available with the skills a specific business needs. Phase 3 refused to instantiate a regional labour-scarcity pressure for exactly this reason: the only state series bundles mining with construction, and no regional measure exists.

records.name: Credit an operating business can draw on to expand
Licences and permissions a business must hold to operate
records.source: documented where it bit: pre-2021 quota liquor licences are recorded as a licence-cost barrier that limited restaurant formation in small towns, and the 2021 reform lowered it
records.observation_required: Which licences the documented transfers and formations actually needed, and which took longest. It is a per-case question, and BF01 and BF13 would surface it.

records.name: Access to inspected meat processing limits how much northern livestock reaches local markets as meat
records.geography: Region-wide; acute in Taos, Santa Fe, Los Alamos (no inspected slaughter), Mora and San Miguel (ranching counties)
records.behaviour_to_explain: Why does so little northern beef and lamb reach retailers, restaurants and schools as locally processed meat, when the region has substantial cattle inventory?

records.name: Northern produce does not reliably reach northern institutional and retail buyers through intermediated channels
records.geography: Rio Arriba, Taos, Mora, San Miguel and rural Santa Fe County; Santa Fe city is partly served
records.behaviour_to_explain: Why aren't more northern producers selling to institutional and retail buyers in the north, when buyers have NM Grown money and producers are shifting away from direct sales?

records.name: Local wholesale demand depends on time-limited public purchasing programs
records.geography: Region-wide (food banks, schools, senior centres); statewide policy
records.behaviour_to_explain: Why is intermediated local demand fragile, growing while programs run and exposed when they end?

records.name: The producer base is ageing and contracting faster than new operators enter
records.geography: Region-wide; steepest farm-count declines in San Miguel, Sandoval, Mora, Taos
records.behaviour_to_explain: Why are operations exiting and producers ageing, and why don't new growers replace them?

records.name: Water and climate volatility make northern supply unreliable year to year
records.geography: Region-wide; exceptional drought now concentrated in Santa Fe County; wildfire exposure highest in Mora, Taos, Colfax
records.behaviour_to_explain: Why can't buyers count on stable local volume, and why do production measures swing between census years?

records.name: Rural grocery in single-store valleys fails store by store
records.geography: Northern Taos County (Questa), Mora, Rio Arriba valleys (Dixon, Chama, Española area), Los Alamos (co-op)
records.behaviour_to_explain: Why do rural northern communities lose their only full grocery store, and why do replacements depend on grants?

records.name: Shared food infrastructure is concentrated in few operators and fails its users when governance fails
records.geography: Taos County (TCEDC); counties with no licensed shared kitchen (Los Alamos, Mora, San Miguel, Sandoval); Colfax (planned)
records.behaviour_to_explain: Why do shared kitchens and processing assets built with public money under-serve food businesses?

records.name: Thin margins and episodic grant capital limit investment and ownership transition in small food businesses
records.behaviour_to_explain: Why don't farms and small food businesses invest in equipment, cold storage or acquisitions, and why do owner exits end in closure?

records.name: Institutional demand is fragmented into small awards and filtered through kitchen capacity and food-service contracts
records.geography: Northern school districts (Española, Taos, Pojoaque, Questa, Mora, Chama, Peñasco), senior centres, hospitals, LANL
records.behaviour_to_explain: Why does local share of institutional food purchasing vary so much across northern buyers, and why are large buyers (hospitals, LANL) absent?

records.question: How do population change and labour supply reach the region's capacity to build, care, produce and sell — and what does that do to households?

records.name: Tight credit
records.duration_required: two consecutive quarters of net tightening, with risk pricing above its recent norm

records.name: Water stress, New Mexico
records.duration_required: 12 consecutive weeks with at least half the state in D2 or worse

records.name: Personal Economic Gain
records.definition: the financial benefit an individual receives through participation in an economic system
records.why_not_a_strength_score: PEG is what a system DELIVERS to a person. System strength is the system's capacity to produce. A place can raise one and not the other, and R3.6 observed exactly that: Los Alamos real median income did not move while production doubled.
records.status: not measured as such; no held source reports an individual's gain from participation

records.name: Quality of Life
records.definition: people's ability to access resources and meet financial, cognitive, affective, spiritual and other needs
records.status: not measured; the held sources carry income, rent and employment, which are inputs to it and are not it

records.name: Household financial buffer
records.definition: recurring disposable resources − necessary recurring costs
records.identity: true by construction; it carries no empirical content until BOTH terms are observed for the same household, period and geography
records.status: neither term is held at household level. ACS medians are DIFFERENT HOUSEHOLDS: the median-income household is not the median-rent household, so differencing the two medians does not produce any household's buffer.
